case_title: Tekan alias Tekram v. State of Madhya Pradesh (now Chhattisgarh)
accused_occupation: Not stated as an occupation; judgment says inherited ancestral land of about 2 acres is his source of livelihood
accused_socioeconomic_status: Better placed than the victim: owns inherited ancestral land (about 2 acres), lives in a pucca house, and his wife holds a blue card
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance: friend of the victim's brother, who visited the victim's house and was in conversation with her
evidence_type: Victim testimony (PW-1); medical examination and doctor's report (Ex.P2, P3); radiologist's X-ray age report (Ex.P4); evidence of Panchayat attendees
confession: Extra-judicial admission before the village Panchayat, as alleged by the prosecution; the Supreme Court did not separately analyse it and upheld conviction on the overall evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Victim blind and illiterate; sexual intercourse obtained on a promise of marriage; repeated intercourse when victim was alone; victim became pregnant
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.376; sentenced to 7 years rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Criminal Appeal No. 2554 of 1997 dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed
neutral_facts: The victim, who is blind and illiterate, lived in her family home with her brothers after her mother left. The accused, a friend of one of the victim's brothers, began visiting the house and talking with the victim. The prosecution case is that about a year before the incident the accused came to the house when the victim was alone, said he loved her and would marry her, and wanted intercourse. The victim tried to avoid it because she was blind, but she submitted after being assured of marriage and support. The accused then came to the house whenever the victim was alone and had intercourse with her. When the victim became pregnant and asked him to marry her, he stopped visiting. The incident was disclosed to the victim's father, who called a village Panchayat. There the accused admitted having had intercourse with the victim but refused to marry her and left. The prosecution's case is that, though blind, the victim could recognise the accused by voice and touch. The matter was investigated, the victim was medically examined, and a charge-sheet was filed. Prosecution witnesses included the victim, a doctor who gave the medical examination report, a radiologist whose X-ray examination estimated the victim's age at approximately 18 years, and persons who attended the Panchayat. The victim testified that she recognised the accused by his voice, that he committed intercourse with her on the pretext of marriage, and that he stopped visiting after she became pregnant. She also testified that the Panchayat was held after she disclosed the incident.
physical_harm: No physical injury recorded in the judgment; victim became pregnant as a result of the intercourse
premeditation_planning: No explicit finding of premeditation; the Supreme Court described the conduct as malicious and fraudulent, using a promise of marriage to commit rape
motive: alleged: sexual gratification obtained through a promise of marriage
key_evidence_accepted: Overall evidence considered by both courts, including the victim's testimony (PW-1), medical evidence, radiological age evidence and Panchayat evidence; the Supreme Court found no infirmity
witness_credibility: Not separately discussed; the Supreme Court said it meticulously examined the two courts' findings and held guilt proved beyond reasonable doubt
post_offence_conduct: Admitted intercourse before the Panchayat, refused to marry, and stopped visiting the house after the victim became pregnant
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: 29.11.1997; High Court: 16.01.2014; Supreme Court: 11.02.2016
legal_representation: Appellant (accused): D. Bharat Kumar, Vikranth Nilesh Goyal (for Vishal Arun). State: Atul Jha, Sandeep Jha (for Dharmendra Kumar Sinha)
investigation_status: Investigated by police; victim medically examined; charge-sheet filed under s.376 IPC; prosecution witnesses examined; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.376 IPC, 7 years RI. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: State counsel placed the Chhattisgarh Victim Compensation Scheme before the Court and, on instructions, proposed sheltering the victim in Nari Niketan with food, clothes, shelter and her Rs.300 monthly pension. No specific argument on guilt is recorded
legal_principle_applied: Victim compensation under s.357A CrPC and rehabilitation of rape victims; guilt proved beyond reasonable doubt on the evidence; a uniform compensation scheme is needed
precedent_relied_upon: Delhi Domestic Working Women's Forum vs. Union of India and Ors., Writ Petition (Crl) No. 362/93 (NCW rape-victim relief scheme, revised 15 April 2010)
sentencing_rationale: Not stated; the Supreme Court did not discuss the sentence and dismissed the appeal, upholding the 7-year term
judicial_aggravating_factors: Victim's physical disability and social disadvantage were exploited; the victim was put in a doubly disadvantaged situation; she has suffered since the crime
other_sentence_order: State to pay Rs.8,000 per month as victim compensation till the victim's lifetime, treated as interest on a Rs.10,00,000 fixed deposit, with no lump sum. All States and Union Territories directed to endeavour to formulate a uniform rape-victim compensation scheme for physically handicapped women
